subject: MAP alignment and commercial redlines — ramp triggers / true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Lisa Torres <lisa.torres@acme-analytics.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: t.ellis@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot MAP + timeline — need alignment on commits and pricing

Jonas — thanks again for yesterday's demo. We want to formalize an evaluation MAP so execs can sign off. Key asks: a 90-day eval, milestone-based pricing/credits, and clarity on how usage is defined for true-ups. Our procurement will need a cadence for commits vs actuals and a price-protection clause for model upgrades.

Could you share a draft MAP and high-level commercial guardrails today? We want the finance team to model the ramp (months 0–6) and the potential true-up exposure.

Attachments: none from our side yet.

—Lisa
Lisa Torres
VP Product, Acme Analytics
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Torres <lisa.torres@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP + timeline — need alignment on commits and pricing

Thanks Lisa — great to hear. I've attached a one-page MAP (20251103_acme_map_v1.xlsx) and a short pricing summary. High-level proposal:

- Evaluation: 90 days, up to 1M tokens of hosted inference included as evaluation credits.
- MAP milestones:
  1) Week 2: Integration complete + smoke test (no commercial swap)
  2) Week 6: Eval milestone — 10k monthly active requests; if met, unlock 15% pilot discount for months 2–3
  3) Day 90: Ramp acceptance — production readiness signoff triggers transition to committed plan
- Commercial transition: a 6-month ramp plan with staged commits: 0.5x month1, 1x month2–3, 2x month4–6 (commits represent anticipated average monthly tokens).
- True-up: quarterly true-up to reconcile committed tokens vs actual usage, with a 10% grace band before charges.
- Price protection: existing committed unit price held for 12 months post-contract; upgrades to materially newer model families (e.g., moving to next-gen architecture) are subject to review and potential repricing; propose explicit carve-outs for forced security/bug fix releases.

I'll loop Marissa and Neha for commercial/legal redlines — I flagged the true-up and definitions of "billable token" as areas we'll likely need tighter phrasing.

Next steps: please confirm MAP milestones and whether Acme wants the price-protection window extended to 18 months; we'll circulate a redline-ready clause for your counsel.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Pilot MAP + timeline — need alignment on commits and pricing

Looping in for operational sizing and pricing guidance. Quick notes:

- The proposed 1M eval credit is generous; recommend we keep it but gate larger eval consumption behind advance notice so Dedicated capacity scheduling isn't impacted.
- Ramp commits look reasonable; suggest adding a clause for burst capacity (10% of committed tokens per month) billed at a premium rate rather than forcing immediate true-up.
- On price protection: 12 months is fine for model parity — do not extend to 18 months without Legal ok; longer protections limit our ability to pass on quantization and perf-driven savings.

I'll draft pricing scenarios vs ARR impact for the next call. Attaching a compact pricing summary (redwood_pricing_summary_v3.pdf).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, GTM Finance | Redwood Inference
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 14:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP + timeline — need alignment on commits and pricing

Thanks for the context. I'm proposing a few contract redlines to protect both parties and keep economics predictable. Draft language attached (acme_trueup_redline_draft.docx). Key points: 

1) Definition of Billable Usage — explicit counting rules: input + output tokens, multi-party calls, and retries within 5 minutes counted once; exclude developer test keys for first 30 days.
2) True-up mechanics — quarterly reconciliation with a one-time administrative cap fee; any overage beyond 15% of committed volume in a quarter converts to overage charges at the committed rate (not list).
3) Price protection — lock-in at committed unit price for 12 months; allow step-downs if we introduce cheaper quantized variants at parity; step-ups require 30 days' notice and a migration plan.
4) Credits/discount clawback — if MAP milestones are not met due to customer delays (integration or data issues), we reserve the right to revoke a portion of pilot discounts retroactively.

Ask Legal to sign off on the proposed up/down migration language. Also want to add an explicit "MAP termination" trigger if after 90 days integration hasn't made production progress — that avoids open-ended eval consumption.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Torres <lisa.torres@acme-analytics.com>, t.ellis@acme-analytics.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Updated MAP & redline summary — actions and timing

Lisa / Tom — attaching the MAP and a redline summary per our internal review (see attachments). Short summary of changes we propose based on your ask and our legal/commercial guardrails: 

- MAP: 90-day eval remains. We set explicit integration and acceptance milestones at day 14 and day 45 to gate commercial discounts.
- Eval credits: 1M tokens included; excessive consumption (above 1.25M) requires prior notice and may be throttled or billed at pilot overage rate.
- Ramp & commits: staged commits as discussed; we added a 10% monthly burst allowance billed at 150% rate to avoid immediate true-ups for small spikes.
- True-up language: quarterly reconciliation; 15% grace band; overages billed at committed unit price unless customer exceeds 200% of committed volume in a quarter — then apply escalated pricing.
- Billable usage: agreed to explicit token rules (input + output) and exclusion for test keys first 30 days.
- Price protection: 12 months for committed price; we will include a clause that allows step-downs for cheaper parity variants and requires 30 days' notice for price increases tied to new major model families.

Requested next actions from Acme:
1) Confirm acceptance of the 12-month price-protection window or propose 18 months and highlight which models must be protected.
2) Confirm whether procurement needs the burst allowance removed or prefer a true-up-only path.
3) Share counsel's preferred language for "billable usage" if Acme has a standard definition.

Proposed timeline: we circulate a negotiated commercial term sheet by 11/14; legal redlines finalized by 11/21 to keep on track for a 12/1 target go-live.

If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk through the redlines.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
